newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish cabinet readies European integration plan.
newsitem.headline: Polish cabinet readies European integration plan.

text.p: The Polish government will finish work on a strategic programme for integration with the European Union by early 1997, Finance Minister Grzegorz Kolodko said on Friday.

"The government...is preparing the National Integration Programme, aimed at bringing Poland into the EU, which will be presented to parliament at the beginning of 1997," Kolodko told a news conference.

He said his "Euro 2006," a long-term scheme designed to adjust Poland's economy to prepare for joining the community's economic and monetary union (EMU) within 10 years, should be discussed by the government in December.
Poland hopes to begin EU accession negotiations by early 1998 and join the community shortly after the year 2000.

The European Union has suggested that Poland, along with the Czech Republic and Hungary, could be among the first former Soviet-bloc countries to join the EU but said its entry was unlikely before 2002.

Kolodko said his anti-inflationary "Euro 2006" scheme was meant to adjust the economy, by 2004, to meet the EU's five so-called Maastricht criteria, which concern the public debt, budget deficit, inflation, interest and foreign exchange rates.
The programme, details of which Kolodko has not yet revealed, will provide for lowering annual inflation to five percent in 2000 and three percent in 2003 from the current 19.5 percent.
Kolodko earlier said he would like Poland to join the EMU between 2006 and 2008.
